title: Building a second MLflow task set at another base commit
answers: How do I make a benchmark task set at a different base commit?
How do I clone the mlflow bundle for a bench variant?
What flags does mlflow-tasks build take?
body:
- Clone from the bundle into a new dir under `bench/repos`: `git clone bench/data/mlflow-upstream.bundle bench/repos/<name>`.
- Pick the base as the first-parent commit before a date: `git rev-list -1 --first-parent --before=<ISO date> origin/master` (run in the clone).
- Build tasks with `node bench/mlflow-tasks.js build <prs.json> --clone <dir-under-repos> --out <name> --base <sha>`. `--clone` and `--out` select a second clone and its own task file; the default is `repos/mlflow`.
- `--hard` keeps only candidates with at least 120 changed lines or at least two source files (test files excluded from the count).
- The build is slow (preflight per candidate); run it in the background.
applies: For the MLflow bench task generator only; the default run uses the original clone and no flags.

search: For MLflow benchmark task generation, building a secondary task set at a custom base commit requires cloning bench/data/mlflow-upstream.bundle into bench/repos/<name>. Tasks are built with node bench/mlflow-tasks.js build <prs.json> --clone <dir-under-repos> --out <name> --base <sha>, using git rev-list to find the base commit. The --hard flag filters candidates to those with at least 120 changed lines or two source files, and builds should run in the background due to preflight slowness.
